info.name: Apiconfy
info.description:
API collection for Apiconfy integration runtime.

## Setup
1. Start the server with `pnpm dev` (install dependencies with pnpm only).
2. Set base_url (default http://localhost:3000) and api_key if API_KEY is configured.
3. REST > Invoke folders run in order: registration, invocation, execution lookup. Invoke scripts save execution_id. Execution recording is queued off the response path, so an execution-lookup request run immediately after invoke can occasionally 404 — rerun it once if that happens (Newman users: add a short delay or a retry-on-404 script).
4. Complex/error examples use upstream_url (default https://httpbin.org). Use dummy data only, or your own httpbin-compatible upstream.

## Structure — by component type
Health and Service Management retain existing requests. REST includes registration plus Phase 2 Invoke > Simple Examples, Complex Examples, Error Cases. `auth.basic` and `auth.oauth2` execute (the REST component fetches and caches the token and replays once on a 401); `auth.jwt` registrations are registration-only and invoking them returns 501. TLS registrations (`request.ssl`, `disableSSL`) are executable since Phase 3.6, and a dedicated REST > Auth folder holds the auth examples — auth payloads must satisfy the Phase 4 schema because registration validates them (`auth.jwt` execution is the remaining Phase 4 work). Runnable Phase 2 complex examples include every supported section and intentionally omit unsupported capabilities. Payload validation (request.validation.fields) is part of every complex example and has dedicated manual examples under REST > Payload Validation; the future component folders show the same block in their own sections. Mapper, Database, Script and SQS are future Phase 11 designs, not registered handlers in Phase 2; Scheduler is Phase 10.

## Data bag
The invoke request body is the context itself — send the API payload as-is. Wrapping it as `{ "context": { ... } }` is also accepted and unwrapped (a few examples show this form). Invoke success is `{ data }`; failure is `{ error: { code, message, details } }`; the execution id is returned in the `Execution-Id` response header. The HTTP status carries success or failure, and upstream failures expose the upstream response as `error.details.body`. Input uses {$context.*}; ephemeral raw upstream response uses {$output.*}. Response transformations wrap output under unique keys. Phase 2 returns transformed output directly and leaves context.output empty; callers must not supply context.output. Transformation still runs on failure: wire data is null, while GET /api/v1/executions/{{execution_id}} exposes the sanitized transformed, error-injected result. Merging into {$context.output.<uniqueKey>} is Phase 5 workflow behavior.

## Limits
Only timeout.response is enforced, per attempt through body consumption. `auth.jwt` (registration validates it; execution is pending), connect/socket/idle (post-v1 — Bun's fetch exposes no per-request control for them), circuitBreaker and unsupported content types return 501. `request.ssl` and `disableSSL` execute since Phase 3.6, and `auth.ssl` governs the token endpoint. Phase 2 implementation verification is pending; this collection is not test-run evidence.

item.name: REST
item.description: REST is the only implemented component type. Existing Complex Examples with `auth.jwt`, circuitBreaker or connect/socket/idle timeouts are REGISTRATION-ONLY: invocation returns 501 (`auth.basic`, `auth.oauth2` and TLS execute). Invoke contains runnable Phase 2 examples with every supported config section; unsupported sections are intentionally omitted. Phase 2 final verification is pending. Never send real secrets to the public example upstream.

item.name: Invoke
item.description: Run each folder in order: register before invoke. Simple Examples use local /health. Complex and selected error examples require an httpbin-compatible upstream_url; default is public httpbin.org, so use dummy data only. Each invoke saves execution_id. Failures return only `error` on the wire; execution lookup exposes the sanitized transformed error-injected result. No workflow context merge in Phase 2. Payload validation runs before dispatch (after condition); see REST > Payload Validation for manual examples of request.validation.fields.

item.name: Payload Validation
item.description: Manual request.validation.fields examples (not part of the automated collection runner): required, type, minItems, minLength, wildcard array-element checks and quoted keys. Run against a live server after the registration below — invalid payloads return 400 with attempts=0 and zero upstream requests.

body.raw: {"service":"phase2-validation","action":"validated","componentType":"rest","description":"Payload validation showcase with every request.validation.fields feature","config":{"request":{"uri":"{{upstream_url}}/anything","method":"POST","contentType":"application/json","validation":{"fields":[{"path":"userId","required":true,"type":"string"},{"path":"customer.email","required":true,"type":"string","minLength":1},{"path":"items","required":true,"type":"array","minItems":1,"message":"items must contain at least one entry"},{"path":"items[*].sku","required":true,"type":"string"},{"path":"items[*].qty","type":"integer"},{"path":"meta[\"external-id\"]","required":true,"type":"string"}]},"payloadTemplate":{"customerId":"{$context.userId}","email":"{$context.customer.email}","items":"{$context.items}"}},"timeout":{"response":5000},"output":{"transformation":{"validatedResponse":{"customerId":"{$output.json.customerId}"}}}}}

request.description: Expected 201/200. One entry per validation feature: required + type, minLength, minItems, wildcard element rule and the quoted key meta["external-id"]. Payload paths are the caller payload's own fields — never context.* or {$...}.
Expected 200; data.validatedResponse.customerId is the mapped payload value. Validation passed before the upstream call.
VALIDATION_FAILED: userId must be a string. Strict typing — a number is not accepted for a string field.
VALIDATION_FAILED: items must contain at least one entry. required accepts [], so emptiness needs minItems; wildcard element rules pass vacuously on an empty array.
VALIDATION_FAILED: customer.email must have at least 1 character. required accepts "", so blank strings need minLength.
VALIDATION_FAILED with the concrete element index: path ["items", 1, "sku"], message "items[1].sku is required". Wildcard rules report the first failing element only.

item.name: TLS Certificates
item.description: Trust a private CA for an HTTPS API with `request.ssl.ca` (inline text or `{$env.NAME}`; no file paths). Give one entry per certificate file: PEM text (starts with `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`) or, for a binary DER `.cer`, its base64 (`base64 -w0 file.cer`). `ca` must include the self-signed root; the root alone is enough when the server sends its intermediates, otherwise add the issuing CA(s). `ca` replaces the default CA list for that request. mTLS: add `cert` + `key` (PEM only) and optional `passphrase` next to `ca`. `ca`, `cert`, `key` and `passphrase` may each be `"{$env.NAME}"` (resolved at invocation; the variable can hold real newlines or literal `\n`). `ssl.disableSSL: true` skips verification and can only be used on its own. The certificates below are throwaway examples — replace them with your own.

item.name: Register — trust a private CA (ssl.ca list)

request.description: Simple: one certificate file per list entry. Returns 201.

item.name: Register — ssl.ca with PEM text and base64 DER

request.description: Complex: a PEM leaf plus the base64 of a binary DER root (`base64 -w0 root.cer`). The `ssl` block is read from the stored component on every invocation. Returns 201.
Skips certificate verification for this component in every environment (no production guard). Only valid on its own. Returns 201.

item.name: Register — complex: private CA chain + mTLS with full config

request.description: Complex: request headers/payload from `$.context`, `ssl.ca` list (root + issuing CA, one entry per certificate file), client `cert` + `key` for mutual TLS, retry, response validation and a uniquely keyed transformation. Returns 201.

item.name: Register — complex: mTLS with encrypted key and passphrase

request.description: Complex: an encrypted PKCS#8 private key (`-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----`) with its `passphrase`, and a base64-DER root next to a PEM one. The passphrase is masked in logs and API responses. Returns 201.

item.name: Register — complex: ca, cert, key and passphrase from env

request.description: Complex: all TLS material is supplied through `{$env.NAME}` (choose inline or env per field). Env-supplied values can't be checked at registration: a missing variable gives 500 ENV_REF_UNRESOLVED and invalid or root-less material gives 502 when invoked. Returns 201.

item.name: Update — rotate ssl.ca at runtime (next invocation uses it)

request.description: PUT the first complex example with `version: 1` (optimistic locking) and a changed `ssl.ca`. TLS material is read from the stored component on every invocation, so no restart is needed: the next invoke trusts only the new CA. Returns 200.

item.name: Register — complex: disableSSL with retry and transformation

request.description: Complex: skip verification for a test partner endpoint while keeping payload mapping, retry and response transformation. `disableSSL` cannot be combined with `ca`/`cert`/`key`. Returns 201.
A lone server/intermediate certificate is not a trust anchor (unlike a Java keystore): include the chain up to the self-signed root. Returns 400.
`ssl.disableSSL: true` cannot be combined with `ca`, `cert` or `key`. Returns 400.
`cert` and `key` go together (mTLS). Returns 400.
Expected PEM or base64-encoded DER. Returns 400.
`{$env.}` is not a valid reference — expected `{$env.NAME}`. Returns 400.
`passphrase` only applies together with `key`. Returns 400.

body.raw: { "service": "auth-demo", "action": "basic_post", "componentType": "rest", "description": "Minimal basic auth: username + password. The password is an {$env} reference so it never reaches the database as a literal.", "config": { "request": { "uri": "{{upstream_url}}/post", "method": "POST", "auth": { "basic": { "username": "svc-account", "password": "{$env.DEMO_PASSWORD}" } } } } }

request.description: Expected 201. Required keys: `username`, `password`. `username` must not contain `:` (the Basic credential separator, RFC 7617). Executes at invoke time (sent as `Authorization: Basic base64(username:password)`). Read it back via GET to see the password masked as `***`.

body.raw: { "service": "auth-demo", "action": "oauth2_post", "componentType": "rest", "description": "Minimal OAuth2 client_credentials: no scope, default client authentication (HTTP Basic).", "config": { "request": { "uri": "{{upstream_url}}/post", "method": "POST", "auth": { "oauth2": { "clientId": "{$env.ORDER_API_CLIENT_ID}", "clientSecret": "{$env.ORDER_API_CLIENT_SECRET}", "accessTokenUri": "https://auth.example.com/oauth/token" } } } } }

request.description: Expected 201. Required keys: `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `accessTokenUri`. `accessTokenUri` must be absolute `https://` (or an `{$env.NAME}` reference) — client credentials travel over it and RFC 6749 §2.3.1 requires TLS. `disableSSL` means "do not verify the certificate", never "send it in cleartext".

Executes the basic_post registration. The runtime builds `Authorization: Basic base64(username:password)` from the config (the password is resolved from `DEMO_PASSWORD` on the server) and forwards the body as-is. Set `DEMO_PASSWORD` in the server environment first.

Executes the oauth2_post registration. The runtime fetches a token from `accessTokenUri` with client_credentials, caches it, sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and replays once if the upstream answers 401. The caller never supplies a token. Point `accessTokenUri` at a real IdP and set `ORDER_API_CLIENT_ID` / `ORDER_API_CLIENT_SECRET` on the server first.

item.name: Register — complex: Okta-style client_credentials (Basic auth, scope list, audience)

request.description: Expected 201. `clientAuth: "basic"` puts the credentials in `Authorization: Basic …` (RFC 6749 §2.3.1 — the shape the Okta-style endpoint in the estate uses). `scope` is ONE space-delimited string (13 `ek.*` scopes in the real call; shortened here) and is omitted entirely when empty. `audience` is the extra token-request parameter Okta needs when the API's `aud` is not the auth server default — the decoded access token carries `aud: api://skywards`. `auth.ssl` is the TOKEN ENDPOINT's TLS policy (a different host from `request.uri`), not the API call's; `request.ssl` still governs the API call. `ssl.disableSSL` cannot be combined with `ca`/`cert`/`key`.

item.name: Register — complex: SiteMinder-style client_credentials (credentials in the body)

request.description: Expected 201. Both client-auth shapes exist in the estate, which is why `clientAuth` exists at all. `clientAuth` defaults to `basic` — if the IdP expects the credentials in the body and returns 401, set `clientAuth: "body"` (the error carries that hint). Sending both at once is forbidden by RFC 6749 §2.3.1. This endpoint returns no `scope`, and that is fine — a token response may omit it (§5.1). Chart the flow: cache a token, reuse it across calls, and on a 401 invalidate, re-acquire and replay the request once.

item.name: Register — complex: jwt.external legacy token fetch

request.description: Expected 201. Required keys: `username`, `password`, `accessTokenUri`. Optional with defaults: `credentialPlacement` (`body`), `contentType` (form-urlencoded), `requestBody` (extra params — it must NOT redefine `username`/`password`, which come from the block fields), `responsePath` (`access_token`; a missing path is an error, never an empty token), `requestHeader` (`Authorization`), `tokenPrefix` (`Bearer ` — an empty string is legal, as here, for a bare custom header). The name is misleading: RFC 7523's JWT grant carries a signed `assertion`, which this is not. `disableSSL` is no longer accepted here — it lives in `auth.ssl`.

item.name: Register — complex: jwt.local signed JWT with claims

request.description: Expected 201. Required keys: `algorithm` (`HS256`/`HS384`/`HS512`/`RS256` — `none` is not expressible), `secretOrPrivateKey`. An inline HS* key must be at least 32 bytes (RFC 7518 §3.1); an `{$env.NAME}` reference is length-checked at invoke. `claims` + `expiresInSeconds` (default 300) are what make the JWT acceptable to a real IdP — without them it carries no `exp` and is a non-expiring credential. `secretOrPrivateKey` is name-masked on read: a literal comes back `***`.
Expected 400. `accessTokenUri` must be absolute `https://` or an `{$env.NAME}` reference. `disableSSL` skips certificate VERIFICATION; it never permits cleartext.
Expected 400. RFC 7518 §3.1 requires an HMAC key at least the size of the hash output. The message names the 32-byte minimum.
Expected 400. Credentials come from the block fields; a duplicate in `requestBody` hides which one wins.

Expected 400 (unknown key — the objects are strict). Token-endpoint TLS was hoisted to `auth.ssl`, which already carries `disableSSL`; write `"auth": { "ssl": { "disableSSL": true }, "jwt": { … } }` instead. There is exactly one auth block per component, so there is exactly one token endpoint to configure.
Expected 400. At most one of `basic`, `oauth2` or `jwt`; within `jwt`, exactly one of `external` or `local`.
Returns 400 with `VALIDATION_FAILED` and field-level details.
Returns 400 — `request.uri` is required for REST components.
Returns 400 — request.method must be GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE.
Returns 400 — `request.disableSSL` and `request.ssl` are mutually exclusive.
